title: What continuing education does MSRB Rule G-3 require of municipal advisors and dealers?
description: MSRB Rule G-3 continuing education for municipal advisors: annual needs analysis, written training plan, fiduciary duty content, records, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board (MSRB) Rule G-3(i)(ii) requires every municipal advisor to evaluate and prioritize its training needs at least annually, develop a written training plan, and conduct training annually for its municipal advisor representatives and principals. Training must cover fiduciary duty obligations owed to municipal entity clients and applicable regulatory requirements. Dealers have a parallel Firm Element duty under G-3(i)(i)(B). There is no minimum hours requirement.
keyTakeaways: Rule G-3(i)(ii)(B)(1) sets a three-part annual cycle for municipal advisors: evaluate and prioritize training needs, develop a written training plan, and conduct training on municipal advisory activities.
Rule G-3(i)(ii)(B)(2) requires training on at least two matters: fiduciary duty obligations owed to municipal entity clients, and applicable regulatory requirements.
The municipal advisor continuing education requirement took effect January 1, 2018, under amendments the SEC approved in May 2017 (82 FR 23394).

Municipal advisors must keep records of program content and completion by covered persons under G-3(i)(ii)(B)(3) and Rule G-8(h), and Rule G-9(h) generally requires five-year retention of G-8(h) records.
A firm that is both a dealer and a municipal advisor may use a single written training plan if it is consistent with both needs analyses, under G-3(i)(ii)(E).
regulator: Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board (MSRB); examination by FINRA for its members and by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for other municipal advisors
appliesTo: Municipal advisors registered with the SEC and the MSRB
Municipal advisor representatives and municipal advisor principals ("covered persons" under G-3(i)(ii)(A))
Brokers, dealers and municipal securities dealers, for the Regulatory Element and Firm Element under G-3(i)(i)
Dealer-municipal advisors that choose a combined training plan under G-3(i)(ii)(E)

sections.heading: Who must meet the Rule G-3 continuing education requirements?

blocks.text: [MSRB Rule G-3](https://www.msrb.org/Rules-and-Interpretations/MSRB-Rules/General/Rule-G-3), on professional qualification requirements, contains two continuing education regimes in paragraph (i). Paragraph (i)(i) covers brokers, dealers and municipal securities dealers and their registered persons. Paragraph (i)(ii) covers municipal advisors and their "covered persons," defined as any person qualified as a municipal advisor representative or municipal advisor principal.

Not every employee is in scope. The MSRB's [FAQs on continuing education for municipal advisors](https://www.msrb.org/Regulation-and-Compliance/FAQs-Continuing-Education-Program-Requirements-Municipal-Advisors) answer that annual training is not required for all employees, but all covered persons must participate in the firm's program. This page states the position as at November 2026; the most recent G-3 amendment listed in the MSRB's rule history is MSRB Notice 2023-07 (September 12, 2023).

sections.heading: What does the annual needs analysis and training plan cycle involve?

blocks.text: Rule G-3(i)(ii)(B)(1) requires each municipal advisor to maintain a continuing and current education program for its covered persons and, at a minimum, to do three things at least annually. The rule text reads:

blocks.title: MSRB Rule G-3(i)(ii)(B)(1)
blocks.text: "At a minimum, each municipal advisor shall at least annually evaluate and prioritize its training needs, develop a written training plan, and conduct training annually on municipal advisory activities for covered persons. The plan must take into consideration the municipal advisor's size, organizational structure, and scope of municipal advisory activities, as well as regulatory developments."

The MSRB's resource [Developing a CE Needs Analysis and Written Training Plan](https://www.msrb.org/Regulation-and-Compliance/Developing-a-CE-Needs-Analysis-and-Written-Training-Plan) (October 2017) describes the same cycle as three steps: conduct a needs analysis that evaluates and prioritizes training needs; develop a written training plan based on those needs; and deliver training each year in accordance with both. The resource notes that the needs analysis must be documented and should reflect the information gathered and the firm's analysis. The method is close to a standard [training needs analysis](/glossary/training-needs-analysis), applied to a regulated population.

sections.heading: What should a municipal advisor's needs analysis consider?

blocks.text: The MSRB's sample checklist groups the inputs into an organizational assessment and other considerations. The organizational assessment covers firm structure (for example, sole practitioner or multi-person firm, other registrations as an investment adviser or broker-dealer, disciplinary or legal history), firm activities (advice on issuance, municipal financial products, investment of proceeds, solicitation), types of clients, and covered persons' knowledge, experience and disciplinary history.

The other considerations look for evidence of training needs: risks in the products and services the firm advises on, recent regulatory developments such as rule amendments, guidance, enforcement actions and examination reports, changes to firm policies, supervisory reviews showing procedures are not being followed, the annual review of compliance policies and supervisory procedures under Rule G-44, client feedback, and feedback from regulatory exams. For a general method, see [how to conduct a training needs analysis](/guides/how-to-conduct-a-training-needs-analysis).

sections.heading: What must municipal advisor training cover?

blocks.text: Rule G-3(i)(ii)(B)(2) requires programs to be appropriate for the firm's business and, at a minimum, to cover two matters concerning the municipal advisory activities, services and strategies the firm offers: fiduciary duty obligations owed to municipal entity clients, and applicable regulatory requirements.

Fiduciary duty training is required even if the firm has no municipal entity clients today. The MSRB's FAQs explain that registration and qualification do not limit the type of client a municipal advisor may serve, so even firms that do not currently advise municipal entities have the potential to do so. Firms do, however, have flexibility over the scope of that training.

Rule G-3(h)(ii)(G) gives a useful indication of what the MSRB treats as core content. For an individual returning under the requalification exemption, the municipal advisor must provide continuing education covering at least the principles of fair dealing; Rules G-20 (gifts and gratuities), G-37 (political contributions), G-40 (advertising by municipal advisors) and G-8 (books and records); the core conduct standards of Rule G-42 for non-solicitor municipal advisors or Rule G-46 for solicitor municipal advisors; and rule changes since the person was last associated. Those topics are a reasonable starting list for any annual plan.

sections.heading: How does the dealer Firm Element under G-3 differ?

blocks.text: Dealers follow the same annual pattern, applied to municipal securities. Under G-3(i)(i)(B)(2)(a), each broker, dealer and municipal securities dealer must at least annually evaluate and prioritize its training needs, develop a written training plan, and conduct training annually on municipal securities for registered persons. The plan must consider size, structure, scope of business, regulatory developments and the performance of registered persons in the Regulatory Element.

Dealer training must cover topics related to the role, activities or responsibilities of the registered person and to professional responsibility. G-3(i)(i)(B)(2)(d) lets dealers count AML compliance training and annual compliance training required by a registered securities association toward the Firm Element. For FINRA members those are the [Rule 3310 AML training](/regulations/finra-rule-3310-aml-program-training) and the [Rule 3110 annual compliance meeting](/regulations/finra-rule-3110-annual-compliance-meeting). The FINRA side of continuing education is on the [FINRA continuing education requirements](/regulations/finra-continuing-education-requirements) page.
The Regulatory Element is separate. Under G-3(i)(i)(A), covered registered persons complete the Regulatory Element for each registration category annually by December 31.

sections.heading: What records and delivery methods are acceptable?

blocks.text: Rule G-3(i)(ii)(B)(3) requires a municipal advisor to administer its program in line with its annual evaluation and written plan and to maintain records documenting program content and completion by covered persons. The SEC order approving the requirement, published at [82 FR 23394](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2017/05/22/2017-10303/self-regulatory-organizations-municipal-securities-rulemaking-board-order-granting-approval-of-a) on May 22, 2017, describes the companion Rule G-8(h) amendments requiring records of the needs analysis, the written training plan, training content and completion, and notes that Rule G-9(h) generally requires G-8(h) records to be preserved for not less than five years.

Delivery is flexible. The MSRB FAQs confirm there is no minimum hour requirement, that firms can use webinars, e-learning and podcasts, including free and low-cost trade association and MSRB resources, and that materials from a webinar attended by one covered person can be circulated to others. In that case the MSRB suggests the firm may want written acknowledgement of receipt and review from each recipient. The person administering the program need not be a principal, and the function can be outsourced, but the firm keeps ultimate responsibility.

sections.heading: How can a firm map G-3 duties to roles, timing and evidence?

blocks.text: The table below is an original planning aid that maps each G-3 continuing education duty to the people it covers, the timing the rule sets, and the evidence an examiner would reasonably expect to see.

blocks.text: The 2018 transition is a reminder that the three steps are sequential. When the requirement took effect on January 1, 2018, the MSRB FAQs confirmed that firms had until December 31, 2018 to complete the first needs analysis, written plan and training. Each later year should show the same order: analysis, then plan, then delivery. See [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry treats the G-3 needs analysis as the framework itself: firm activities, client types and applicable MSRB rules are mapped to covered persons before any training plan is drafted. The written plan and each year's content then trace back to that map, which makes the annual cycle visible to an examiner. See the [financial services](/industries/financial-services) page.

faqs.q: Is there a minimum number of hours for municipal advisor continuing education?
faqs.a: No. The MSRB's FAQs state that Rule G-3 does not set a minimum hour requirement for a municipal advisor's continuing education program. The amount of training should follow from the firm's documented needs analysis and written training plan.

faqs.q: Do municipal advisor principals need different training?
faqs.a: Not by rule. The MSRB FAQs say firms are not required to provide specialized training to municipal advisor principals, but a firm's needs analysis may show that specific training is appropriate, for example on the supervisory obligations of municipal advisors.

faqs.q: Can a sole proprietor municipal advisor use free resources?
faqs.a: Yes. The MSRB FAQs say sole proprietors have flexibility over content and delivery and need not develop in-house materials. They may use existing content, including free and low-cost resources from trade associations and the MSRB, if it meets the firm's needs analysis.

faqs.q: Who examines municipal advisors for continuing education compliance?
faqs.a: Rule G-3(i)(ii)(D) refers to the appropriate examining authority: a registered securities association for municipal advisors that are its members, and the SEC or its designee for other municipal advisors. In practice that means FINRA for FINRA members and the SEC for others.

factCheck.claim: Rule G-3(i)(ii)(B)(1) requires each municipal advisor at least annually to evaluate and prioritize training needs, develop a written training plan, and conduct training annually on municipal advisory activities for covered persons, considering size, structure, scope of activities and regulatory developments.
Rule G-3(i)(ii)(B)(2) requires training to cover, at a minimum, fiduciary duty obligations owed to municipal entity clients and applicable regulatory requirements.

Rule G-3(i)(ii)(E) permits a dealer-municipal advisor to use a single written training plan consistent with both needs analyses; G-3(i)(i)(B)(2)(d) allows dealers to count AML and annual compliance training toward the Firm Element.

The MSRB FAQs state the implementation date was January 1, 2018, firms had until December 31, 2018 for the first cycle, there is no minimum hour requirement, and fiduciary duty training is required even without current municipal entity clients.
The MSRB needs analysis resource describes a three-step annual process (needs analysis, written training plan, delivery) and states the needs analysis must be documented.

The SEC approval order (82 FR 23394, May 22, 2017) describes Rule G-8(h) recordkeeping for the needs analysis, plan, content and completion, and notes Rule G-9(h) generally requires five-year preservation.

Rule G-3(h)(ii)(G) lists minimum continuing education topics for the requalification exemption: fair dealing; Rules G-20, G-37, G-40 and G-8; G-42 or G-46 core obligations; and intervening rule changes.
